prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1442; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road and said the other vehicle drifted into their lane. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and was willing to speak directly.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it, with coverage in force at the time of the loss. No indication the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 3: Police report lists the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the scene, and the responding officer's notes match the claimant's account of the lane change.

Entry 4: Received photos from the claimant showing the driver's side panels. The images confirm the general area of contact, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle with the appraiser. The damage pattern matches the impact described, and a few older scratches on the rear quarter panel may predate this crash and will be noted separately in the estimate.

Entry 6: Claimant reported neck and lower back discomfort the day after the collision and was seen at urgent care. The reported injury, a back strain, fits the kind and force of a sideswipe at this speed.

Entry 7: Obtained treatment records. Care followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication, with visit frequency tapering as the claimant's symptoms improved.

Entry 8: Prior records show a small strain in the same area several years ago, which resolved fully with conservative care. The current complaint is being evaluated in that context.

Entry 9: Spoke with the claimant again to review timeline and sequence of events. The account matched the initial statement in every conversation, with no material differences in the description of the lane change.

Entry 10: Requested the other driver's statement and contacted the reporting officer for any additional scene notes. File remains open pending receipt of the treatment summary and the final repair estimate.

Entry 11: Reviewed the full file with the supervisor. Liability and damage appear consistent with the reported loss, and the claim will proceed to settlement evaluation once the medical summary is complete.
